title: Can Klarna Buy Now Pay Later Be Wiped Out in Bankruptcy?
summary: A bankruptcy attorney explains how Affirm, Klarna, and PayPal installment debts are treated in bankruptcy filings.

assertions.quote: The buy now, pay later type loans—they can be included in the bankruptcy
the CLA, the PayPal, the Affirm—they don't show up on your credit report

verdicts.note: Matches the pattern that many BNPL providers historically didn't report to credit bureaus, so attorneys can miss these debts unless specifically told about them.
CFPB: BNPL lenders 'historically have not furnished loan performance data to the credit bureaus,' consistent with these accounts often not appearing on a standard credit report.

assertions.quote: once you decide to file bankruptcy, don't go out and rack up your credit card debt and your buy now, pay later stuff

verdicts.note: Consistent with general bankruptcy law on fraudulent pre-filing debt accumulation, which applies to any new credit use, not just BNPL specifically.

assertions.quote: the overarching rule is: any debt that you had prior to that bankruptcy gets discharged in that bankruptcy, even if you don't list it

verdicts.note: In a no-asset Chapter 7, pre-filing debts are generally discharged even if unlisted, though an unlisted debt can still cause practical complications like a later lawsuit.
